raw_response:
I've been farming this land for over fifty years. My father farmed it before me. I know what grows here in Quzhou — wheat in winter, corn in summer. That's the rotation. That's what makes sense. The grain station takes both. My neighbors all do the same. I'm not going to try something new at my age.

My two kids are in the city now, so I'm managing about ten mu myself, maybe with my wife helping during busy times. Ten mu is enough for me to handle. I won't take on more — my back isn't what it was.

For wheat, I'll go to the seed shop and get the improved variety they recommend — probably 矮抗58 or whatever the extension station is pushing this year. I trust those. I tried traditional seed years ago but yields were always lower. I put down compound fertilizer as a base when I plant, then top-dress with urea in spring when the plants green up. I water at least three times — before the ground freezes, again in March when growth picks back up, and once more around heading. I spray herbicide in early spring before the weeds get out of hand, and I'll spray for aphids closer to harvest if I see them.

For the summer corn, I plant right after the wheat comes off in June. Hybrid seed — 郑单958, same as always, reliable. I throw on a big bag of urea at the jointing stage, that's the main feeding. Corn doesn't need much else from me. Two irrigations if the summer is dry. Herbicide right after emergence, one more spray if the armyworm shows up.

I use the rotary tiller both times. The plow is too much work now, and rotary is fine for our soil.
